overview: A Pacific storm brings snow to the Utah and Wyoming mountains through Friday and Saturday, then a weaker system clips northern Utah on Monday. Southwest and central Colorado see showers and cold air through the weekend, and a wet pattern is expected to return to the West late next week.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A Pacific storm system brings snow to Utah's mountains through early Saturday, focused on the north as it goes. Winds from the southwest favor the northern Utah peaks. Powder Mountain leads with 10" and is under a Winter Storm Warning from Thursday night to Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 12 to 20 inches Friday through Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A storm moves across Wyoming and Montana, with the heaviest snow west of the Divide and on the mountain passes. Grand Targhee leads with 10" and is under a Winter Weather Advisory from Thursday night to Friday night. Jackson Hole has similar showers. The NWS is calling for more at Grand Targhee, 7 to 17 inches Friday through Monday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Southwest winds carry moisture over the Colorado high country tonight into Saturday, with snow showers in the mountains and light accumulation in high valleys. Telluride and Crested Butte both show 7" through Monday. Gusty winds reach 50 mph in Telluride on Friday. Snow squalls are possible along I-70 Friday morning, though confidence is low.

ahead.text: The Climate Prediction Center expects a wet pattern to return to the West next week, with storms possible through the week of November 25.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
